name: Ted the Caver
title: The Diary That Stopped Updating in May 2001
claims: "Ted the Caver" is a short horror story self-published on an Angelfire website in 2001 | 1
It is presented as the online diary of a man who excavates an unexplored cave with friends | 1
A free website on Angelfire; free website-building services in the late 1990s let anyone build sites | 1
First entry dated 23 March 2001, final entry 19 May 2001 | 1
One later account (Screen Rant) gives the year as 2000 | 2
Narrator refuses to disclose names or locations for the apparent safety of readers | 1
Ted and friend "B" find a small hole in the local "Mystery Cave" | 1
The hole leads to a tight passage they dub "Floyd's Tomb" before opening up further | 1
They hear a scream and the sound of rock scraping from within the hole | 1
The pair spend days tirelessly excavating the opening | 1
Ted encounters strange hieroglyphs | 1
The scraping source is a round rock formation that moves to reveal a new passage | 1
Ted and B ascend terrified as they feel their rope being pulled back into the cave | 1
Another caver, Joe, is traumatized in the cave and refuses to elaborate on what he saw | 1
Ted experiences nightmares and hallucinations | 1
Ted writes that they will bring a gun into the cave among other supplies; blog not updated since | 1
Irregular real-time updates gave readers the impression of witnessing events as they happened (Crawford) | 1
Images were linked rather than embedded, common to reduce load times; Crawford thought it gave apprehension; none of the images are disturbing | 1
Final entry only became "final" retroactively after readers gave up hope (Crawford) | 1
Entries link to the next, final hyperlink directs to same page, implying Ted had been killed by the entity | 1
Romano: obsessed narrator who keeps returning to danger, supernatural entity in unsettling setting, ambiguous ending are tropes | 1
Message boards constantly debated authenticity; some users thought it true due to images and details | 1
A group of cavers identified "Mystery Cave" as an actual cave in Utah | 1
"The Fear of Darkness" by Thomas Lera was shared by some as a completed version; it was fan-made and explained elements left a mystery | 1
After several years the author resurfaced and said it was based on his real caving experiences with many fictional additions | 1
Bloody Disgusting's writer compared it to The Blair Witch Project; fear reduced but it "stands on its own" as an effective, old-fashioned supernatural mystery | 1
Sometimes considered the first creepypasta; Daily Dot's Aja Romano wrote it "may be the earliest viral example" | 1
Academic Tosha R. Taylor said it did not go viral but remained in spaces dedicated to gothic discussions where it is still circulated | 1

Influenced Marble Hornets ("Entry #26", 2010) use of live updates; "The Dionaea House" spread across multiple blogs updated in real time, with comment-section communication, and gave greater authenticity; SCP Foundation influenced | 1
Living Dark: The Story of Ted the Caver (2013), loosely based; two estranged brothers reunite after father's funeral to explore a cave | 1
Originally produced in 2008; released for theatres and video on demand on 2 October 2015 | 1
Screen Rant in 2020 called it solid but lacking the psychological tension, with an ineffectual twist | 1, 2
Screen Rant said in 2020 the original Angelfire page was still up | 2
Official website listed as not accessible as of May 17, 2026; Internet Archive copy exists | 1
